At a grand banquet he pointed at Fan Aineng and several others and rebuked them: "You are veteran generals of successive reigns, not men who cannot fight—yet you fell back because you wished to sell me to Liu Chong like goods on the market.
units.literal: Returning in triumph, he halted at Luzhou and wished to take by surprise those who had retreated in defeat. He set a grand banquet and, pointing at Fan Aineng and several others, rebuked them: "You are all veteran generals of successive reigns, not men unable to use troops—yet you fell back for no other reason than truly wishing to sell me as merchandise to Liu Chong.

units.zh: 言訖，命行刑壯士擒出皆斬之。
units.en: When he had finished, executioners seized them and all were beheaded.
units.literal: When he had spoken, he ordered executioners to seize them and all were beheaded.

units.zh: 史臣曰：世宗頃在仄微，尤務韜晦，及天命有屬，嗣守鴻業，不日破高平之陣，逾年復秦、鳳之封，江北、燕南，取之如拾芥，神武雄略，乃一代之英主也。
units.en: The historian writes: Shizong was lately in obscurity and practiced concealment; when Heaven's mandate fell to him, he inherited the great enterprise. Within days he broke the Gaoping line; within a year he recovered Qin and Feng. North of the Yangzi and south of Yan he took territory as one picks up mustard seeds. Divine in martial prowess and heroic in strategy, he was the heroic ruler of his age.
units.literal: The historian says: Shizong was lately in low estate and especially practiced concealment; when Heaven's mandate was his, he succeeded to the great enterprise. Within days he broke the Gaoping line; within a year he recovered the territories of Qin and Feng. North of the Yangzi and south of Yan he took lands as one picks up mustard seeds. Divine in martial prowess and heroic in strategy, he was an heroic ruler of a generation.

units.zh: 然稟性傷於太察，用刑失於太峻，及事行之後，亦多自追悔。
units.en: Yet his nature was marred by excessive keenness of perception, and his punishments erred on the side of severity; after the fact he often regretted them himself.
units.literal: Yet his inborn nature suffered from excessive keenness of perception, and his use of punishments erred on the side of severity; after matters were carried out, he often regretted them himself.

units.zh: 甲戌，詔：「每年新及第進士及諸科聞喜宴，宜令宣徽院指揮排比。」
units.en: On jiaxu, an edict ordered: "Each year the celebratory banquet for newly passed jinshi and other examination graduates be arranged under the direction of the Palace Domestic Service."
units.literal: On jiaxu, an edict stated: "Each year the celebratory banquet for newly passed jinshi and candidates of other examination categories should be arranged under the direction of the Palace Domestic Service."

units.zh: 乙亥，詔：「禮部貢院今後及第舉人，依逐科等第定人數姓名，並所試文學奏聞，候敕下放榜」云。
units.en: On yihai, a further edict declared: "Henceforth successful candidates at the Ministry of Rites examination compound must have their numbers and names set by rank within each category, with their examination essays reported to the throne; the list is to be posted only after imperial approval."
units.literal: On yihai, an edict stated: "Henceforth successful candidates at the Ministry of Rites examination compound shall have their numbers and names fixed by rank within each category, together with their examination compositions reported to the throne, and the list shall be posted only after an imperial order."

units.zh: 永德對以群臣之意皆願為此，世宗熟思久之，嘆曰：「吾固知汝必為人所教，獨不喻吾意哉！
units.en: Yongde replied that all the officials wished it. Shizong thought long and sighed: "I knew someone had coached you—you alone fail to grasp what I mean!
units.literal: Yongde replied that all the officials wished this. Shizong pondered long and sighed: "I knew all along that someone must have coached you—you alone fail to grasp my intent!

units.zh: 然觀汝之窮薄，惡足當此！」
units.en: Yet look at your meager means—how could you be fit for such a role!"
units.literal: Yet looking at your paltry resources, how could you be equal to this!"

units.zh: 不然，何寡人親戰而劉崇始敗耶？
units.en: Otherwise, why was Liu Chong defeated only when I fought in person?
units.literal: Otherwise, why was it only when I fought in person that Liu Chong was first defeated?

units.zh: 如此則卿等雖萬死不足以謝天下，宜其曲膝引頸以待斧誅。」
units.en: For this, ten thousand deaths would not suffice to answer to the realm; bend your knees and offer your necks to the axe."
units.literal: In such a case, though you died ten thousand deaths it would not suffice to answer to the realm; you should bend your knees and stretch your necks to await the axe."

units.zh: 世宗謂之曰：「汝江南自以為唐之後，衣冠禮樂世無比，何故與寡人隔一帶水，更不發一使奉書相問，惟泛海以通契丹，舍內事外，禮將安在？
units.en: Shizong said to them: "You of Jiangnan call yourselves heirs of Tang, with rites and music unmatched in the age—yet separated from me by only a strip of water, you send no envoy with a letter of greeting, but cross the sea to deal with the Khitan, abandoning kin for outsiders. Where is propriety in that?
units.literal: Shizong said to them: "You of Jiangnan consider yourselves heirs of Tang, with rites and music unmatched in the age—why then, separated from me by only a belt of water, do you not send a single envoy with a letter of inquiry, but cross the sea to communicate with the Khitan, abandoning the inner for the outer? Where is propriety?

units.zh: 今又聞汝以詞說寡人罷兵，是將寡人比六國時一群癡漢，何不知人之甚也！
units.en: Now I hear you use words to persuade me to halt the army—you take me for one of the witless lords of the Warring States. How little you know your man!
units.literal: Now I hear you use words to persuade me to halt the army—you take me for one of the witless fools of the Six States era. How greatly you misjudge men!

units.zh: 汝慎勿言，當速歸報汝主，令徑來跪寡人兩拜，則無事矣。
units.en: Say no more. Return at once and tell your lord to come straightway and kneel before me in two prostrations, and all will be well.
units.literal: Take care not to speak further. Return quickly and report to your lord: let him come straightway and kneel before me in two prostrations, and all will be well.

units.zh: 不然，則寡人須看金陵城，借府庫以犒軍，汝等得無悔乎！」
units.en: Otherwise I shall have to visit Jinling and borrow its treasury to reward my army—will you not regret it!"
units.literal: Otherwise I must visit Jinling city and borrow its treasury to reward the army—will you not regret it!"

units.zh: 未幾，賜之書：「敕陳摶，朕以汝高謝人寰，棲心物外，養太浩自然之氣，應少微處士之星，既不屈於王侯，遂甘隱於巖壑，樂我中和之化，慶乎下武之期，而能遠涉山塗，暫來城闕，浹旬延遇，宏益居多，白雲暫駐於帝鄉，好爵難縻於達士。
units.en: Before long he granted him a letter: "To Chen Tuan: You have loftily withdrawn from the world and dwell beyond things, nurturing primordial breath and answering to the star of the recluse. Refusing princes, you hide in cliffs and ravines, delighting in our culture of harmony and rejoicing in this age of martial virtue; yet you crossed mountain paths to visit the capital. For more than ten days we received you, and the benefit was mostly ours. White clouds briefly rested at court; fine rank cannot bind the man of attainment.
units.literal: Before long he granted him a letter: "Imperial order to Chen Tuan: We hold that you have loftily withdrawn from the human realm and dwell with heart beyond things, nurturing the breath of great primordial nature and answering to the star of the Recluse of Shaowei. Having refused to bow to princes and lords, you gladly hide in cliffs and ravines, delighting in our culture of central harmony and rejoicing in the age when martial virtue descends; yet you could traverse mountain paths and come briefly to the capital. For more than ten days we received you, and the great benefit was mostly ours. White clouds briefly rested in the imperial domain; fine rank cannot bind the man of attainment.

units.zh: 昔唐堯之至聖，有巢、許為外臣，朕雖寡薄，庶遵前鑒。
units.en: Of old the sage Yao had Youchao and Xu as ministers beyond the court; We, though meager, would follow that example.
units.literal: Of old the utmost sage Yao of Tang had Youchao and Xu as outer ministers; We, though meager, would follow that earlier mirror.

units.zh: 恐山中所闕，已令華州刺史每事供須。
units.en: Fearing want in the mountains, We have ordered the prefect of Huazhou to supply your every need.
units.literal: Fearing want in the mountains, We have ordered the Huazhou prefect to supply your every need.

units.zh: 乍反故山，履茲春序，緬懷高尚，當適所宜，故茲撫問，想宜知悉。」
units.en: Having returned to your mountain in this spring season, We think fondly of your lofty withdrawal, which suits you well; therefore We send this greeting—may you know Our mind."
units.literal: Having suddenly returned to your old mountain, treading this spring season, We think fondly of your lofty withdrawal, which should suit you well; therefore We send this inquiry of care—may you know Our mind."

units.zh: 世宗以張昭遠好古直，甚重之，因問曰：「朕欲一賢相，卿試為言朝廷誰可。」
units.en: Shizong greatly valued Zhang Zhaoyuan for his love of antiquity and upright character and asked: "I want a worthy grand councilor. Tell me who in court will serve."
units.literal: Shizong, because Zhang Zhaoyuan loved antiquity and was upright, greatly valued him and asked: "I desire one worthy grand councilor. Try telling me who in court will do."

units.zh: 世宗常薄濤之為人，聞昭遠之舉甚驚，曰：「李濤本非重厚，朕以為無大臣體，卿首舉此何也？」
units.en: Shizong had always disdained Tao's character; hearing the recommendation he was surprised and said: "Li Tao is not grave by nature; I consider him without the bearing of a great minister. Why recommend him first?"
units.literal: Shizong had always held Tao's character in low esteem; hearing Zhaoyuan's recommendation he was greatly surprised and said: "Li Tao is by nature not grave and weighty; I consider him without the bearing of a great minister. Why do you first recommend this man?"

units.zh: 世宗曰：「今卿言甚公，然此人終不可於中書安置。」
units.en: Shizong said: "What you say is fair, yet this man can never be placed in the Secretariat."
units.literal: Shizong said: "What you say now is very fair, yet this man can in the end not be placed in the Secretariat."

units.zh: 世宗志在四方，常恐運祚速而功業不就，以王樸精究術數，一旦從容問之曰：「朕當得幾年？」
units.en: Shizong's ambition lay in the four quarters; he often feared his allotted years would pass before his work was done. Because Wang Pu was expert in divination, one day he asked him casually: "How many years shall I have?"
units.literal: Shizong's ambition lay in the four quarters; he often feared that fortune would pass swiftly and his achievements not be completed. Because Wang Pu was expert in numbers and fate, one day he asked him at ease: "How many years shall I have?"

units.zh: 世宗喜曰：「若如卿言，寡人當以十年開拓天下，十年養百姓，十年致太平足矣。」
units.en: Shizong rejoiced and said: "If it is as you say, I shall use ten years to conquer the realm, ten years to nurture the people, and ten years to bring great peace—that will suffice."
units.literal: Shizong rejoiced and said: "If it is as you say, I shall use ten years to open and expand the realm, ten years to nurture the people, and ten years to bring great peace—that will suffice."

units.zh: 及瓦橋不豫之際，復夢向之神人來索傘與經，夢中還之而驚起，謂近侍曰：「吾夢不祥，豈非天命將去耶！」
units.en: When he fell ill at Waqiao, he dreamed again that the divine man came to reclaim the umbrella and the classic; in the dream he returned them and woke in alarm, telling his attendants: "My dream is ill-omened—is Heaven's mandate about to depart!"
units.literal: When he fell ill at Waqiao, he again dreamed that the former divine man came to demand back the umbrella and the classic; in the dream he returned them and started up in alarm, saying to his close attendants: "My dream is ill-omened—is not the Mandate of Heaven about to depart!"

units.zh: 乙丑，賜諸將射於內鞠場。
units.en: On yichou, the Emperor granted the generals an archery contest in the inner polo ground.
units.literal: On yichou, the generals were granted archery in the inner polo ground.

units.zh: 戊辰，幸迎春苑。
units.en: On wuchen, the Emperor visited Yingchun Park.
units.literal: On wuchen, he visited Yingchun Park.

units.zh: 辛丑，幸迎春苑。
units.en: On xinchou, the Emperor again visited Yingchun Park.
units.literal: On xinchou, he visited Yingchun Park.

units.zh: 甲子，詔以北境未復，取此月內幸滄州。
units.en: On jiazi, an edict announced that because the northern frontier had not yet been recovered, the Emperor would visit Cangzhou before the month was out.
units.literal: On jiazi, an edict stated that because the northern frontier had not yet been recovered, within this month he would visit Cangzhou.

units.zh: 丁酉，駕御龍舟，率舟師順流而北，首尾數十里。
units.en: On dingyou, the Emperor boarded his dragon boat and led the fleet downstream; the column stretched bow to stern for several tens of li.
units.literal: On dingyou, he boarded the dragon boat and led the fleet downstream to the north; bow to stern the line stretched several tens of li.

units.zh: 壬寅，宿於野次。
units.en: On renyin, the Emperor encamped in the open field.
units.literal: On renyin, he lodged in an open camp.

units.zh: 時帝先期而至，大軍未集，隨駕之士不及一旅，賴今上率材官騎士以衛乘輿。
units.en: The Emperor had arrived ahead of the main army; those with the imperial train numbered less than a regiment. The present sovereign led the skilled cavalry to guard the imperial carriage.
units.literal: At that time the Emperor had arrived ahead of schedule; the main army had not yet assembled, and those accompanying him did not amount to a full regiment. It was thanks to the present sovereign leading the skilled cavalry officers to guard the imperial carriage.

units.zh: 世宗北征，將兵至瓦橋關，內斌為關使，開門請降，世宗以為汝州刺史。）〉
units.en: When Shizong campaigned north and brought troops to Waqiao Pass, Neibin was pass commander; he opened the gate and offered surrender, and Shizong appointed him prefect of Ru.)〉
units.literal: When Shizong campaigned north and led troops to Waqiao Pass, Neibin was pass commander; he opened the gate and requested surrender, and Shizong made him prefect of Ru.)〉

units.zh: 五月乙巳朔，帝駐蹕於瓦橋關。
units.en: On the first day of the fifth month, yisi, the Emperor halted at Waqiao Pass.
units.literal: In the fifth month, on yisi the first day of the month, the Emperor halted the imperial procession at Waqiao Pass.

units.zh: 丙午，帝與諸將議攻幽州，諸將皆以為未可，帝不聽。
units.en: On bingwu, the Emperor consulted the generals about attacking Youzhou; they all urged that the time was not right, but he would not heed them.
units.literal: On bingwu, the Emperor discussed with the generals an attack on Youzhou; the generals all held that it was not yet feasible, but the Emperor would not listen.

units.zh: 是夜，帝不豫，乃止。
units.en: That night the Emperor fell ill, and the attack was called off.
units.literal: That night the Emperor fell ill, and the plan was halted.

units.zh: 泉州節度使劉從效遣別駕王禹錫奉貢於行在，帝以泉州比臣江南，李景方歸奉國家，不欲奪其所屬，但錫詔褒美而已。
units.en: Liu Congxiao of Quanzhou sent Vice Prefect Wang Yuxi with tribute to the temporary court. The Emperor judged that Quanzhou stood in the same relation as a Jiangnan subject, and since Li Jing had only just returned to allegiance, he did not wish to seize another's domain and merely issued an edict of commendation.
units.literal: Quanzhou Military Commissioner Liu Congxiao sent Vice Prefect Wang Yuxi to present tribute at the temporary court. The Emperor held that Quanzhou was comparable to a subject of Jiangnan, and Li Jing had just returned to allegiance to the state; he did not wish to seize what belonged to another and merely granted an edict of praise.

units.zh: 甲戌，上至自雄州。
units.en: On jiaxu, the Emperor returned from Xiong Prefecture.
units.literal: On jiaxu, the Emperor returned from Xiong Prefecture.

units.zh: 永德然之，乘間為世宗言如群臣旨，世宗問：「誰使汝為此言？」
units.en: Yongde agreed and at an opportune moment relayed the officials' plea to Shizong. Shizong asked, "Who put you up to this?"
units.literal: Yongde agreed and seized an opportunity to speak to Shizong as the officials wished. Shizong asked: "Who told you to say this?"

units.zh: 帝之北征也，凡供軍之物，皆令自京遞送行在。
units.en: During the northern campaign, all military supplies were relayed from the capital to the temporary court.
units.literal: On the Emperor's northern campaign, all supplies for the army were ordered relayed from the capital to the temporary court.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·張美傳》：美少為三司小吏、澶州糧料使，世宗鎮澶州，每有求取，美悉力應之，及即位，連歲征討，糧饋無乏，美之力也。
units.en: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Mei: Mei began as a petty clerk of the three departments and grain commissary at Chanzhou. While Shizong was stationed there, Mei met every request; after his enthronement, supplies never failed through years of campaigning—thanks to Mei.
units.literal: (Eastern Capital Epitome, Biography of Zhang Mei: in youth Mei was a petty clerk of the Three Departments and grain commissary of Cangzhou. When Shizong was stationed at Cangzhou, whenever he made demands Mei did his utmost to meet them; after the enthronement, year after year of campaigns went without shortage of provisions—Mei's doing.

units.zh: 然每思澶州所為，終不以公忠待之。）〉
units.en: Yet Shizong often recalled what had passed at Chanzhou and never treated him with full trust and favor.)〉
units.literal: Yet he often recalled what had been done at Cangzhou and never treated him with full public loyalty.)〉

units.zh: 至江陵，見有卜者王處士，其術如神，世宗因頡跌氏同往問焉。
units.en: At Jiangling they met a diviner, Recluse Wang, whose skill seemed supernatural; Shizong went with Xiedie to consult him.
units.literal: At Jiangling they saw a diviner, Recluse Wang, whose art was like that of a spirit; Shizong went with Xiedie to consult him.

units.zh: 世宗雖佯為詰責，而私心甚喜。
units.en: Shizong pretended to reprove him but was secretly delighted.
units.literal: Shizong feigned rebuke but inwardly rejoiced greatly.

units.zh: 於逆旅中夜置酒，與頡跌氏半酣，戲曰：「王處士以我當為天子，若一旦到此，足下要何官，請言之。」
units.en: At an inn that night he set out wine and, half drunk with Xiedie, jested: "Recluse Wang says I am destined to be emperor. If that day comes, what office would you want? Tell me plainly."
units.literal: At an inn that night he set out wine and, half drunk with Xiedie, jested: "Recluse Wang says I am destined to be Son of Heaven. If that day should come, what office would you want? Speak plainly."

units.zh: 若大官為天子，某願得京洛稅院足矣。」
units.en: If you become emperor, I would be content with the capital tax bureau."
units.literal: If Your Excellency becomes Son of Heaven, I would be content with the capital tax bureau."

units.zh: 世宗笑曰：「何望之卑耶！」
units.en: Shizong laughed: "How modest your ambition!"
units.literal: Shizong laughed: "How low your ambition!"

units.zh: 親軍帥樊愛能等各退衄，世宗赫怒，躍馬入陣，引五十人直沖崇之牙帳。
units.en: Guard commanders such as Fan Aineng fell back in defeat. Shizong blazed with anger, spurred his horse into the line, and with fifty men charged straight at Chong's headquarters.
units.literal: The guard commanders Fan Aineng and others each fell back in defeat. Shizong blazed with anger, leaped his horse into the battle line, and with fifty men charged straight at Chong's headquarters tent.

units.zh: 初，劉崇求援於契丹，得騎數千，及睹世宗兵少，侮之，曰：「吾觀周師易與爾，契丹之眾宜勿用，但以我軍攻戰，自當萬全。
units.en: Earlier Liu Chong had sought Khitan aid and obtained several thousand horsemen. Seeing Shizong's small force, he despised it and said: "The Zhou army is easy prey. Best not use the Khitan; let my army alone fight and all will be secure.
units.literal: Earlier, Liu Chong had sought aid from the Khitan and obtained several thousand horsemen. Seeing that Shizong's troops were few, he despised them and said: "I see the Zhou army is easy to deal with. The Khitan host had best not be used; let only my army fight, and all will be secure.

units.zh: 洎世宗之陣也，三軍皆賈勇爭進，無不一當百，契丹望而畏之，故不救而崇敗。
units.en: When Shizong formed his line, all three armies vied to advance, each man fighting as ten; the Khitan looked on in fear and did not intervene, and Chong was defeated.
units.literal: When Shizong formed his battle line, the three armies all vied in valor to advance, each man matching a hundred; the Khitan looked on in fear and did not rescue, and Chong was defeated.

units.zh: 論者曰：「世宗患諸將之難制也久矣，思欲誅之，未有其釁，高平之役，可謂天假，故其斬決而無貸焉。
units.en: Commentators say: "Shizong had long chafed at unruly generals and wished to execute them but lacked occasion. The Gaoping campaign was heaven's gift; hence he beheaded them without mercy.
units.literal: Commentators say: "Shizong had long been troubled by the difficulty of controlling his generals and wished to execute them but had no occasion. The Gaoping campaign may be called heaven's gift; hence he beheaded them without mercy.

units.zh: 世宗既下江北，駐蹕於建安，以書召偽主。
units.en: After Shizong had crossed to the north bank of the Yangzi, he halted at Jian'an and summoned the Southern Tang ruler by letter.
units.literal: After Shizong had descended on the north of the Yangzi, he halted at Jian'an and summoned the false ruler by letter.

units.zh: 偽主惶恐，命鐘謨、李德明為使，以見世宗。
units.en: The Southern Tang ruler was alarmed and sent Zhong Mo and Li Deming as envoys to see Shizong.
units.literal: The false ruler was fearful and appointed Zhong Mo and Li Deming as envoys to see Shizong.

units.zh: 德明素有詞辯，以利害說世宗使罷兵。
units.en: Deming was known for eloquence and sought to persuade Shizong by arguments of advantage and harm to halt the campaign.
units.literal: Deming was known for eloquence and sought to persuade Shizong by advantage and harm to halt the army.

units.zh: 世宗且知之，乃盛陳兵師，排旗幟戈戟，為鹿項道以湊禦，然後引德明等入見。
units.en: Shizong already knew this and arrayed his troops in full display, with banners, spears, and halberds, forming an avenue of barriers for the imperial approach before admitting Deming and the others to audience.
units.literal: Shizong already knew this and therefore arrayed his forces in full display, setting out banners, spears, and halberds, forming an avenue of deer-antler barriers for the imperial approach, and only then led Deming and the others in to audience.

units.zh: 及見偽主，具陳世宗英烈之狀，非四方所能敵。
units.en: When they saw their ruler, they described Shizong's heroic bearing in full—not to be matched anywhere under heaven.
units.literal: When they saw the false ruler, they fully described Shizong's heroic and fierce bearing—not to be matched in the four quarters.

units.zh: 世宗許之，因曰：「叛則征，服則懷，寡人之心也。」
units.en: Shizong granted it and said: "Rebellion brings war; submission brings mercy—that is my policy."
units.literal: Shizong granted it and said: "Rebellion brings campaign; submission brings embrace—that is my heart."

units.zh: 論者以世宗加兵於江南，不獨臨之以威，抑亦諭之以禮，可謂得大君之體矣。
units.en: Commentators hold that in bringing force against Jiangnan, Shizong confronted them with might yet also instructed them in propriety—the manner of a great prince.
units.literal: Commentators hold that in applying force to Jiangnan, Shizong not only confronted them with might but also instructed them in propriety—truly the manner of a great prince.

units.zh: 世宗之在位也，以四方未服，思欲牢籠英傑，且以摶曾踐場屋，不得志而隱，必有奇才遠略，於是召到闕下，拜左拾遺。
units.en: While Shizong reigned, with the realm not yet united, he wished to win outstanding men; because Tuan had entered the examinations, failed to advance, and retired, he must possess rare talent—so Tuan was summoned to court and made Left Remonstrance and Policy Adviser.
units.literal: While Shizong held the throne, the four quarters not yet subdued, he wished to win over outstanding men; and because Tuan had once entered the examination halls, failed to achieve his aim, and retired, he must possess rare talent and far-reaching design—therefore he was summoned to court and made Left Remonstrance and Policy Adviser.

units.zh: 摶不就，堅乞歸山，世宗許之。
units.en: Tuan declined and firmly begged to return to the mountains; Shizong granted his request.
units.literal: Tuan would not accept and firmly begged to return to the mountains; Shizong granted it.

units.zh: 初，摶之被召，嘗為詩一章云：「草澤吾皇詔，圖南摶姓陳。
units.en: When Tuan was first summoned, he composed a poem: "From the wilds comes Our Emperor's edict; plotting southward is Chen surnamed Tuan.
units.literal: When Tuan was first summoned, he once composed a poem that said: "From the wilds and marshes comes Our Emperor's edict; plotting southward is Chen surnamed Tuan.

units.zh: 凡濤於閨門之內，不存禮法也如此，世宗以為無大臣體，不復任用，宜哉！
units.en: Such was Tao's disregard for propriety even within the family; that Shizong held him unfit for high office and did not employ him again was fitting!
units.literal: In all such ways Tao within the inner quarters did not preserve ritual law; that Shizong held him without the bearing of a great minister and did not employ him again was fitting!

units.zh: 世宗末年，大舉以取幽州，契丹聞其親征，君臣恐懼，沿邊城壘皆望風而下，凡蕃部之在幽州者，亦連宵遁去。
units.en: In Shizong's last years he launched a great campaign against Youzhou. The Khitan, hearing he was campaigning in person, were terrified; border fortresses submitted at sight, and tribal groups at Youzhou fled overnight.
units.literal: In Shizong's last years he launched a great campaign to take Youzhou. The Khitan, hearing that he was campaigning in person, were fearful in court and country; border fortresses all submitted at the mere sight of the army, and all tribal groups at Youzhou fled by night as well.

units.zh: 頃之，有父老百餘輩持牛酒以獻，世宗問曰：「此地何名？」
units.en: Before long more than a hundred elders came with oxen and wine. Shizong asked: "What is this place called?"
units.literal: Before long more than a hundred elders came bearing oxen and wine as gifts. Shizong asked: "What is this place called?"

units.zh: 先是，世宗之在民間也，常夢神人以大傘見遺，色如郁金，加《道經》一卷，其後遂有天下。
units.en: Earlier, while still a commoner, Shizong often dreamed that a divine man gave him a great umbrella colored like saffron, together with a volume of the Daoist Classic; afterward he came to possess the realm.
units.literal: Earlier, while Shizong was among the people, he often dreamed that a divine man gave him a great umbrella colored like turmeric, together with one volume of the Daoist Classic; afterward he came to possess the realm.

units.zh: 臣下有過，必面折之，常言太祖養成二王之惡，以致君臣之義，不保其終，故帝駕馭豪傑，失則明言之，功則厚賞之，文武參用，莫不服其明而懷其恩也。
units.en: When subordinates erred, he rebuked them to their faces. He often said that Taizu had nurtured the wickedness of the two princes, so that the bond between ruler and minister could not be preserved to the end. Therefore he controlled bold spirits: faults he named plainly, merit he rewarded richly; civil and military alike he employed, and all submitted to his clarity and cherished his grace.
units.literal: When subordinates had faults, he always rebuked them to their faces. He often said that Taizu had nurtured the wickedness of the two princes, so that the righteousness between ruler and minister could not be preserved to the end. Therefore the Emperor controlled bold spirits: when they erred he spoke plainly, when they achieved merit he rewarded them richly; civil and military he employed together, and none failed to submit to his clarity and cherish his grace.

units.zh: 漢之得人，於茲為盛，儒雅則公孫弘、董仲舒、兒寬，篤行則石建、石慶，質直則汲黯、卜式，推賢則韓安國、鄭當時，定令則趙禹、張湯，文章則司馬遷、相如，滑稽則東方朔、枚皋，應對則嚴助、硃買臣，歷數則唐都、洛下閎，協律則李延年，運籌則桑弘羊，奉使則張騫、蘇武，將率則衛青、霍去病，受遺則霍光、金日磾，其餘不可勝紀。
units.en: Never did the dynasty gather talent so thickly: Hong, Dong, and Kuan for classical breadth; the Shi brothers for steadfast service; Ji An and Bu Shi for blunt loyalty; Han Anguo and Zheng Dangshi for lifting others; Zhao Yu and Zhang Tang for codifying law; Sima Qian and Xiangru for voice; jesters Dongfang Shuo and Mei Gao; debaters Yan Zhu and Zhu Maichen; calendar-makers Tang Du and Luoxia Hong; the harmonist Li Yan'nian; the reckoner Sang Hongyang; envoys Zhang Qian and Su Wu; blades Wei Qing and Huo Qubing; regents Huo Guang and Jin Midi—and a cloud of names besides.
units.literal: Thus Han obtained men; at this time it was most flourishing: in Confucian elegance then Gongsun Hong, Dong Zhongshu, Er Kuan; in steadfast conduct then Shi Jian, Shi Qing; in plain straightforwardness then Ji An, Bu Shi; in advancing the worthy then Han Anguo, Zheng Dangshi; in fixing statutes then Zhao Yu, Zhang Tang; in literary composition then Sima Qian, Xiangru; in jest then Dongfang Shuo, Mei Gao; in repartee then Yan Zhu, Zhu Maichen; in calendrical reckoning then Tang Du, Luoxia Hong; in harmonizing pitch then Li Yan'nian; in planning transport then Sang Hongyang; as envoys then Zhang Qian, Su Wu; as generals then Wei Qing, Huo Qubing; as testamentary appointees then Huo Guang, Jin Midi—the rest cannot be fully recorded.

units.zh: 是時，漢興六十餘載，海內艾安，府庫充實，而四夷未賓，制度多闕。
units.en: By then Han had stood sixty years at peace, the vaults were full, but the border tribes still stood outside the rites and many statutes waited to be written.
units.literal: At that time, more than sixty years after Han's rise, within the seas were at peace, granaries and treasuries were full, yet the four barbarians had not submitted and institutions were still largely lacking.
